title: Stock Market Today, Nov. 16: Snap Falls Amid Tech Sector Sell-Off and Ongoing Youth Social Media Addiction Lawsuit Exposure
detail:
Stock Market Today, Nov. 16: Snap Falls Amid Tech Sector Sell-Off and Ongoing Youth Social Media Addiction Lawsuit Exposure
Robert Izquierdo, The Motley Fool
Mon, November 16, 2026 at 4:33 PM CST 3 min read
SNAP
PINS
META
^GSPC
^IXIC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Snap (NYSE:SNAP), a visual messaging and augmented reality social platform, closed at $5.09, down 3.23%. A broader tech sector sell-off added to ongoing concerns around roughly 1,600 active youth social media addiction lawsuits, weighing on shares. Investors continue to watch Snapchat's path toward one billion monthly users and its monetization potential.

Trading volume reached 41.5 million shares, coming in nearly 8.1% above its three-month average of 38.4 million shares. Snap IPO'd in 2017 and has fallen 79% since going public.

How the markets moved today

The S&P 500 (SNPINDEX:^GSPC) fell 1.92% to 7,416, and the Nasdaq Composite (NASDAQINDEX:^IXIC) dropped 2.49% to 24,510. Amid internet communication and social media stocks, Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) closed at $626.41, down 2.38%, while Pinterest (NYSE:PINS) finished at $18.42, down 3.81%, highlighting pressure across digital peers.

What this means for investors

On Monday, Nov. 16, Snap stayed under pressure as roughly 1,600 active youth addiction lawsuits remained a central overhang. That legal risk is keeping investors focused on liability exposure and settlement costs. Moreover, Snap may need to change how its products operate to address concerns around the alleged addictive design and youth mental health risks of its apps. If so, that could impact future user growth or advertising revenues.

In addition to the legal concerns, Snap shares fell as part of a broader Wall Street sell-off in technology stocks. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbed past 5% today as persistent inflation remained a key macroeconomic factor. Higher interest rates put pressure on tech sector stock valuations, especially for lower-margin growth companies like Snap.

Earlier this month, Snap reported third-quarter revenue growth of 14% to $1.72 billion and positive net income. However, Q3 average daily active users in its key North American market fell from 98 million to 92 million year over year. This suggests Snap is struggling to retain users in its most important market.

NEW YORK, Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Direxion, a leading provider of specialized ETFs with approximately $70.8 billion in assets under management (as of September 30, 2026), today announced a partnership with Silvia, Inc. (Nasdaq: SVIA), the first publicly traded agentic finance firm.

Direxion

Through the partnership, Direxion will provide Silvia's users with webinars, content and other resources on pursuing income beyond traditional fixed income strategies, including options-based approaches such as Direxion's Defined Income Boost ETFs, which seek to generate income from stocks many investors already follow: NVIDIA, Tesla, Alphabet, Meta, Palantir and Micron.

"Investors make better decisions when they are well informed, especially on something as important as generating income. We're pleased to partner with Anthony, who clearly shares our passion for education, as illustrated by his mission to build the Silvia platform, which is designed to help investors feel more confident and prepared as they plan for the income they need," said Douglas Yones, Chief Executive Officer at Direxion.

The partnership will launch with an inaugural webinar for Silvia's users on Thursday, November 19, at 2 p.m. ET, featuring a conversation between Anthony Pompliano, Chairman and CEO of Silvia, Inc., and Bilal Little, Global ETF Strategist at Direxion. The partnership will continue into 2027 with additional collaborations in the works.

Silvia was co-founded by Anthony Pompliano, an entrepreneur, investor and best-selling author. "Our mission is to help independent investors make money," said Mr. Pompliano. "Partnering with Direxion on educational content gives our users access to clear, practical information about strategies they may want to evaluate as part of their broader financial picture."

Direxion is best known for its leadership in leveraged and inverse ETFs, particularly in technology, with funds such as the Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull & Bear 3X Shares (SOXL/SOXS), among the most actively traded ETFs globally*, the Direxion Daily TSLA Bull 2X and Bear 1X Shares (TSLL/TSLS), and the Direxion Daily SpaceX Bull & Bear 2X ETFs (LOFF/LOFD). The firm recently announced plans to launch the Direxion Daily Anthropic Bull & Bear 2X ETFs (ANTO/ANTD), expected to begin trading on the first trading day after Anthropic's IPO.

Credit: Gene Medi/NurPhoto

Stocks gapped down at Monday's opening bell after a weekend filled with speculation about the future of the leader of the AI revolution, as Nvidia (NVDA) prepares to report results after Tuesday's closing bell without Jensen Huang. Anthropic is on track to complete its initial public offering (IPO) on Wednesday, while Fed Chair Kevin Warsh suggested the U.S. can't sustain its superpower status without leading on AI.

During opening remarks at a symposium on how artificial intelligence will work its way into the broader economy, Warsh said members of the central bank's research staff are studying what it means for workers, as well as the implications of a burst bubble.

The Fed chair said productivity growth is reasonably strong right now but hasn't broken out, suggesting AI's promise remains further in the future.

As Nick Timiraos of The Wall Street Journal reports, "Warsh's remarks repeatedly cast AI as a question of national power, a theme upon which Fed chairs haven't typically dwelled. He recalled the late economist Robert Mundell calling America's rise as a superpower the most important fact of the 20th century, and said for the U.S. today, 'it is a charge to keep.'"

Focused on the bigger picture, Warsh offered no commentary on recent price action, the short-term trajectory of inflation or the Fed's current stance on interest rates.

Is Jensen Huang still Nvidia's 'key man'?

Nvidia fell another 4.1% amid reports that big players at major Silicon Valley venture capital firms are privately advocating for Jensen Huang's return as CEO. NVDA is now down 10.1% since Huang resigned last Thursday.

Though President Donald Trump, Bill Ackman and Elon Musk have publicly expressed their support for the fallen executive, CNBC says the Nvidia board will not heed their call. The board is already dealing with as complex a succession crisis as you'll find in the real world these days.

Indeed, as Noah Weisberger and Yifei Liu of BCA Research conclude, the surprise exit of a CEO is a meaningfully negative event "particularly if the departure is driven by a legal or ethical issue."

Track all markets on TradingView

Based on a total of 30 cases, Weisberger and Liu found that stocks underperform by about 7% in the month after an unexpected CEO departure, and 70% of them lag. The data show that legal/ethical departures cost about 13%. Stocks recover within a month when the cause of the departure is death or illness.

A large debt obligation and a key merger vote are bearing down on Trump Media & Technology Group (NASDAQ:DJT), and the market is pricing in the strain. Trump Media stock is at $4.10, down 12% in morning trading. Over the past month, the stock has fallen 43%.

Sean Gallup / Getty Images News via Getty Images

Two near-term events sit at the center of the selling at Trump Media. The company carries a convertible-note obligation of $976.8 million with a near-term demand feature. In plain terms, the investors who bought those notes may be able to require repayment in cash, which puts direct pressure on the company's reserves. Shareholders will vote on Trump Media's proposed TAE merger. The deal with fusion energy developer TAE Technologies advanced after the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) declared its registration statement effective on November 5.

Speculative and AI-linked stocks are under pressure to start the week, with technology the weakest sector in a broadly lower market. Rumble (NASDAQ:RUM), operator of the Rumble video platform, is falling almost as hard as Trump Media. By contrast, Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META) is only slightly lower.

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS) shares sank 8% at 10.50 a.m. ET on November 16 in regular trading, as neocloud operators sold off. The Next Web, citing the Wall Street Journal, reported that Nvidia's interim CEO is expected to rein in financing for the AI industry and that Jensen Huang had already told neocloud partners to get customers to pay upfront. Nebius was named as a neocloud Nvidia has invested in.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with NBIS.

Is NBIS fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

The growth is real but capital hungry. Nebius reported third-quarter revenue of $980.8 million, up 571%, including about $325 million of non-recurring revenue, and adjusted EBITDA of $465.8 million. It lifted 2026 capex to about $27 billion and guided 2027 capex to $40 billion to $45 billion. Contracted power exceeds 4 GW, and the company says agreements with Microsoft and Meta can be financed through asset-backed structures.

The 2027 capex plan alone equals roughly 1.4 to 1.5 times Nebius's $29.4 billion market cap, so financing terms matter more than revenue beats. If Nvidia steps back as a backer, lenders and equity buyers must fill the gap. GuruFocus gives Nebius a GF Score of 53/100, reflecting rapid growth offset by weak profitability and a stretched balance sheet. GuruFocus publishes no GF Value for the company. The next marker is any new asset-backed financing tied to the Microsoft and Meta contracts.
